title: What’s Next?
subtitle: Choose your next chapter deliberately
summary: Pip sees a title and a role offering deeper learning. Career choices involve values, environment, relationships, energy, and scope—not one universal ladder. Reflection and investments help Pip compare staying, changing work, or moving employers, then test a next step.

concepts.title: Investment
concepts.body: Pip circles a promotion, then notices it offers little practice in the skill they want. Career investment includes skills, visibility, relationships, experiences, and environments that make opportunities possible. Pip reserves time for distributed-systems experiments beyond responsibilities. The right investment depends on the future being sought; promotion is one possible objective, not the only one. Deliberate practice may open a different door.

steps.text: Pip asks what the next opportunity should make possible.
Choose a future beyond a title alone.
Some opportunities require practice outside current responsibilities.

concepts.title: Fit
concepts.body: The workshop offers Pip autonomy but leaves little energy for learning. A role-fit review counts the good parts as well as the frustrations: what does the job provide, what does it cost, and how does that compare with values, needs, and growth? Staying, renegotiating scope, or moving may each make sense. Neither a particular title nor time served proves the role still fits.

steps.text: Notice both what the workshop provides and what it costs.
Judge fit against personal needs and growth direction.

concepts.title: Options
concepts.body: Three doors appear on Pip’s sketch: deepen the current role, change scope, or leave the organization. Consulting and management offer other possibilities. Each trades learning, impact, stability, and autonomy differently. Pip could stay with the same employer and change the work, or move for something unavailable there. The useful comparison concerns the actual work and environment, not which door carries the most upward-sounding title.

steps.text: Pip keeps several real choices open.
Deepening the current work can be growth.
Compare the actual environment before choosing a new organization or role.

concepts.title: Reflection
concepts.body: Pip cannot draw a perfect career map, so chooses a bounded learning experiment and a review date. Reflection turns experience into information: outcomes, energy, values, and what to become able to do next. Pip remains responsible for career choices and the effects of the software they help create. A small deliberate experiment can reveal more than waiting indefinitely for a flawless long-term plan.

steps.text: Pip starts without pretending to know the perfect long-term route.
Use a review point to choose the next step.

misconceptions.claim: a staff-plus role is mainly about applying a universal formula.
misconceptions.correction: The chapter treats judgment as contextual: identify forces, listen to evidence, and adapt the response to the actual system and people.

misconceptions.claim: A visible activity or artifact proves the work is complete.
misconceptions.correction: Completion requires a useful outcome, shared understanding, and a way to notice whether the decision worked over time.

scenario.title: Choose the next investment
scenario.context: Pip’s visible workshop role leaves no time for distributed-systems depth. A lateral role offers learning but less title recognition. Which investment fits?

options.label: Choose deliberate growth
options.benefit: Pip compares the move against desired capability and values.
options.cost: A learning role may offer less immediate title recognition.
options.consequence: Pip weighs relationships, learning, and energy, then sets a review point rather than treating the move as a guaranteed answer.

options.label: Optimize title alone
options.benefit: Title recognition offers an obvious external signal.
options.cost: The actual work may still conflict with values or energy.
options.consequence: Pip’s title rises while the missing capability and role fit remain unchanged.

scenario.debrief: The next rung is not automatically the next useful step. Pip compares lived work and deliberate learning with the future they actually want.

quiz.question: What can expand your future career options?
options: Waiting for a title to create the skills
Investing in skills, relationships, visibility, and experience
quiz.explanation: Different investments make different opportunities possible.

quiz.question: How should you assess whether to stay in a role?
options: Compare its benefits and costs with your needs and goals
Use tenure alone as the deciding metric
Assume changing companies always creates growth
quiz.explanation: Role fit is contextual; both staying and moving can be good choices.

quiz.question: What is useful when the next career step is unclear?
options: Commit to an irreversible plan immediately
Try a deliberate learning experiment and reflect on it
quiz.explanation: A bounded experiment can supply information about what you want and need next.

exercise.title: Make the next move legible
exercise.prompt: Describe a staff-level decision, the people and terrain involved, and the route by which you will learn whether it worked.

fields.label: When will I review the choice?
fields.placeholder: Name the evidence or conversation that will revisit it.
